title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
source: canonical Merge Two Sorted Lists concept; description, examples, and tests re-authored
description: The inputs are the first nodes of two singly linked lists, each sorted in ascending order. Splice or rebuild the nodes into one ascending list and return its first node. Nodes may be reused; only the values and their order in the result matter. Empty lists are valid inputs.

examples.explanation: The lists interleave cleanly into one ascending chain.
Merging with an empty list returns the other list unchanged.

hints: Both lists only ever advance: the smaller leading node belongs next in the result.
A dummy starting point removes the special case of building the first node.
Keep a tail pointer; repeatedly attach the smaller front node and advance that list. Attach whatever remains at the end.
solution: Walk both lists with a tail pointer, always attaching the smaller leading node, then attach the remainder. Each node is attached once: O(n + m) time, O(1) space.
failureHint: hidden tests include two empty lists and values that interleave unevenly
